issue.title: SASE Symvision rejects the private RecoveryAssessment import in failed-close snapshots
issue.description: Proposed by bob-cli-dp.3 note #2, corroborated by bob-cli-dp.4 notes #1-3 and bob-cli-dp.1 check f0968a143d1d4da7462612bb0baf40c8. At SASE d12d712e79, _failed_close_recovery_assess.py defines class _RecoveryAssessment and _failed_close_recovery_snapshots.py line 11 imports it. ToolRun d6a84ef0ab38f1b655e7569a22f79be8 reproduced the same violation on clean origin/master; independent clean witness 13ea2a464abef73b3eab4bfee9e624d7 makes it KNOWN in later checks. The source dates to dcb7d2a6e7, before B5. bob-cli-cv close note claims the type was made public, but current source and history do not contain that change; cv concerns dirty-tree preservation, not this remaining API visibility defect. Read the Symvision policy, expose the intentionally shared assessment type through a public name and update its consumers, or choose a policy-compliant module boundary. Do not suppress or whitelist the misuse. Run focused failed-close snapshot/recovery tests plus governed check. Same/all-type searches, last-week sweep, and active host epic inspection found no duplicate or causal active owner. Small: the failing import and its intended shared type are identified.

task_type_fields.why_not_flake: Deterministic private cross-module import in current source; phase dp.3 reproduced on clean HEAD and subsequent independent check runs report the same KNOWN witness.

issue.creation_reason: Phase bob-cli-dp.3 proposed this independent lint failure; landing confirms the private cross-module import remains on current SASE master and blocks the repository gate.
